topics.title: 6.1.1 Evaluating Boolean Conditions
topics.summary: An if statement executes its controlled statement when the condition converts to true. Conditions often come from explicit comparisons, such as temperature >= 80. Prefer a comparison that communicates the domain over a numeric value used merely for its zero/nonzero conversion. if (device_count > 0) is usually clearer than if (device_count) in beginner code.

topics.title: 6.1.2 Building Multi-Branch if/else Logic
topics.summary: An if/else if/else chain selects the first matching branch. Ordering therefore matters when conditions overlap. Testing a broad condition such as value >= 50 before value >= 80 prevents the later branch from handling high values. Either order thresholds deliberately or write nonoverlapping intervals.

blocks.text: A final else can state the remaining valid case after earlier checks establish the domain. This is often simpler than repeating every lower bound. Explain why the cases are exhaustive and mutually exclusive. A future maintainer should be able to insert a new threshold without guessing whether two branches are intended to overlap.

blocks.text: An if/else if/else chain selects the first branch whose condition succeeds. This makes branch order part of the policy. If the warning condition is temperature >= 60 and it appears before the critical condition temperature >= 80, a reading of eighty-five will be classified as warning unless the logic accounts for that overlap.

blocks.text: One clear ordering is to reject the invalid domain first, test the most severe valid threshold next, then test the lower threshold, and finally return the normal classification. Another valid design uses nonoverlapping intervals. The best choice is the one whose relationship to the decision table is easiest to inspect.

blocks.text: Independent if statements mean something different. A report could legitimately show several independent facts about the same device: it is overdue for calibration and its battery is low. In that case, executing more than one branch is appropriate. A single exclusive temperature label, however, calls for mutually exclusive selection. Do not choose between these structures solely because one uses fewer lines.

blocks.text: Draw the intervals on paper. For this chapter, valid readings zero through fifty-nine are normal, sixty through seventy-nine are warning, and eighty through one hundred fifty are critical. Values outside the valid domain are invalid. Testing fifty-nine, sixty, seventy-nine, and eighty is more informative than testing four random interior values because those cases challenge exactly where responsibility changes from one branch to another.

topics.title: 6.2.1 Building switch Statements
topics.summary: A switch selects among case labels based on an integral or enumeration value. It is well suited to discrete commands and states, not arbitrary ranges or string comparison. Each case label identifies a constant value. A default branch can handle values not otherwise listed, but a default that silently accepts an invalid command defeats input validation.

topics.title: 6.2.2 Understanding Fallthrough and break
topics.summary: Execution can continue from one case into the following case unless a control transfer stops it. break exits the nearest enclosing switch or loop; return exits the function. Unintended fallthrough is a common defect because the source visually resembles a list of independent branches.

blocks.text: Intentional fallthrough can share behavior, but it should be obvious. Use the standard [[fallthrough]]; annotation where appropriate to communicate that decision and assist diagnostics. Do not use it to hide a missing break you have not understood. When each case computes a result, returning that result directly can make the control flow easier to verify than mutating a variable and remembering a break in every branch.

In a switch nested inside a loop, break exits the switch, not the surrounding loop. If a menu’s quit choice must end the loop, use an explicit loop condition or another clearly stated control path. A correct keyword attached to the wrong mental model still produces incorrect behavior.

topics.title: 6.3.1 Simplifying Complex Boolean Expressions
topics.summary: Name meaningful subconditions, remove duplicated comparisons, and use the domain’s structure. A condition such as has_record && is_active && within_limit can express a policy more clearly than a long expression of unrelated field accesses. Negation rules can help simplify logic, but a mathematically shorter expression is not always more readable.

topics.title: 6.3.2 Avoiding Deeply Nested Decision Trees
topics.summary: Early returns can reject invalid input and leave the main path less indented. For example, validate the range, classify the critical threshold, classify the warning threshold, then return normal. This makes each branch’s purpose visible and reduces the amount of state that must be remembered while reading deeper blocks.

blocks.text: Early returns are not an excuse to skip cleanup. At this stage, examples use ordinary values whose lifetimes are automatic. Later, RAII makes resource cleanup follow scope exit even with multiple returns. If a function needs a maze of flags to remember which path was taken, consider dividing it into validation, calculation, and reporting functions with explicit results.

blocks.text: Deep nesting often indicates that the ordinary path is buried beneath repeated validation. Guard clauses can reject invalid cases early, leaving the successful computation at one indentation level. The classification example uses this approach: reject out-of-domain input, then classify known-valid input.

blocks.text: Early return is not automatically superior in every function. Its value depends on whether it makes the function’s responsibilities and cleanup easier to understand. Before resource-owning classes are introduced, several early exits around manually acquired resources can create cleanup mistakes. This is one reason the volume teaches value-based code first and later connects resource lifetime to objects.

topics.title: Evidence beyond a single branch
topics.summary: A good classifier test establishes both coverage and exclusivity. Coverage means every possible input category receives a defined result. Exclusivity means the application does not produce contradictory outcomes for one input when the requirement calls for one label. An if/else chain helps express exclusivity, but it can still encode the wrong priorities.

topics.title: Review and solution reasoning
topics.summary: Why does branch order matter? In an exclusive chain, the first satisfied condition wins. Overlapping conditions therefore encode priority through their position.

cards.question: Why does branch order matter?
cards.answer: In an exclusive chain, the first satisfied condition wins. Overlapping conditions therefore encode priority through their position.

cards.question: When are independent if statements appropriate?
cards.answer: When several facts or actions may legitimately apply to one input. They are not interchangeable with an exclusive classification chain.

cards.question: Why does a default case need a policy?
cards.answer: It receives values outside the named cases. Treating those values as ordinary without justification can conceal malformed or unsupported input.

cards.question: What does break exit?
cards.answer: The innermost loop or switch to which it applies. In a switch inside a loop, it does not automatically end the surrounding loop.

reading.title: Review and solution reasoning
paragraphs: Why does branch order matter? In an exclusive chain, the first satisfied condition wins. Overlapping conditions therefore encode priority through their position.
When are independent if statements appropriate? When several facts or actions may legitimately apply to one input. They are not interchangeable with an exclusive classification chain.
Why does a default case need a policy? It receives values outside the named cases. Treating those values as ordinary without justification can conceal malformed or unsupported input.
What does break exit? The innermost loop or switch to which it applies. In a switch inside a loop, it does not automatically end the surrounding loop.

Chapter takeaway. Conditional logic is a partition of possible states. Make the partition explicit, assign its boundaries deliberately, and test both the selected action and the actions that must not happen.
